story.head: The Bruins hunt better looks than the Blackhawks
paras: The Blackhawks (4-9-0) lost 4-1 to Detroit on Thursday, and the Bruins (9-4-1) lost 4-1 to St. Louis the same night. Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Bruins first in the Atlantic (tied for fourth).

The Blackhawks have played better than their record (.308) says: their chances are worth about .368, and their finishing has held them back. The Bruins’ record (.679) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.555), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Blackhawks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest), don't block many shots (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (32nd). Chicago has scored 2.08 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 3.69, the fourth most. As for the Bruins, they leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest), have had the league’s best goaltending (1st) and sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest). Boston has allowed 2.29 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. The Bruins wait for good looks, but the Blackhawks settle for hopeful ones. Beyond that, the Blackhawks’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot.

Patrick Kane (1 G / 7 A / 8 P in 13 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (5 G / 1 A / 6 P in 13 GP) has a team-high five goals. The Bruins’ scoring runs through David Pastrňák (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 14 GP).
Spencer Knight (4-7-0 / .897 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to go for Chicago. Jeremy Swayman (7-3-1 / .912 SV% in 11 GS) has been a rock in net for Boston and is expected to start.
At home, Marco Sturm likes to send Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Kantserov, Bedard and Teräväinen.
